newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends sharply lower on cash concerns.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends sharply lower on cash concerns.

text.p: Ideas cash lumber may be near or at a top weighed on CME lumber futures and prices ended sharply lower with January again down the daily $10.00 per thousand board feet (tbf) limit in its closing range.

Futures ended $9.90 to $6.00 per tbf lower. November finished off $6.40 at $481.40 after earlier setting a new contract high of $488.00 per tbf. January paced the setback and closed at $407.40 per tbf.
Cold and snowy weather in parts of the Eastern U.S. and record high cash prices slowed cash trade and ideas grew that cash markets may show a correction, traders said.
"The panic buying is over with weather and reality starting to step in," said Roger Champangne, cash dealer with Capital Forest Products Inc.

Champangne noted that the quota on Canadian lumber has added $100 onto the cash price and the market will be correcting itself soon, partly from seasonals and partly from overpriced wood turning buyers off.
Talk circulated on the trading floor that some wholesalers were starting to discount part of their earlier wood purchases to move product, especially with the slower winter demand season arriving.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce unchanged from last Friday at $480 per tbf, the record high. However, January is over $70 under cash which shows that the market expects a big break in the cash market, traders added.
